subject: english-language
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How many separate Speaking and Listening tasks must a candidate complete for CCEA Unit 2?
options: One
Two
Three
Five
questions.explain: Candidates complete three tasks: an individual presentation and interaction, a discussion, and a role play.

questions.q: In the Individual Presentation and Interaction task, what does the 'interaction' element primarily require the candidate to do?
options: Perform a scripted scene with another candidate
Respond to questions and comments after presenting
Write a summary of their talk
Listen silently to a recorded speaker
questions.explain: After delivering the presentation, the candidate must interact by answering questions and responding to points raised.

questions.q: Which variety of English are candidates expected to use in a formal individual presentation?
options: Regional dialect only
Standard English
Text-message abbreviations
A foreign language
questions.explain: Candidates are expected to use Standard English and adapt talk appropriately for formal presentation.

questions.q: A candidate must give an individual presentation on a hobby. Which approach best meets the task's demands?
options: Read the whole talk word-for-word from a full script with no eye contact
Structure the talk with a clear opening, development and conclusion, then answer questions
Speak only in casual slang to seem relaxed
Ask the audience to do the talking for them
questions.explain: A well-structured, sustained talk followed by handling questions fulfils both the presentation and interaction demands.

questions.q: Why is organising a presentation into a clear beginning, middle and end important?
options: It reduces the time the talk takes
It helps the candidate structure and sustain talk so the audience can follow it
It removes the need to use Standard English
It means questions can be avoided
questions.explain: Structuring and sustaining talk so it is clear and purposeful for the audience is a key assessed skill.

questions.q: Why is this task described as an 'individual' presentation?
options: Because the candidate presents alone rather than as part of a group
Because only one mark is available
Because it is completed at home individually
Because it must be about the candidate's own life
questions.explain: The candidate delivers the presentation on their own, in contrast to the group-based discussion task.

questions.q: The Discussion task requires candidates to take part in what kind of activity?
options: A written essay
A group discussion with others
A silent reading test
A solo monologue
questions.explain: The discussion task assesses candidates interacting with others in a group conversation.

questions.q: How should a candidate best demonstrate listening in a discussion?
options: By repeating their own point until others agree
By responding to and building on the ideas of other speakers
By staying completely silent throughout
By interrupting each speaker before they finish
questions.explain: Listening and responding to others' ideas and perspectives is central to the discussion assessment.

questions.q: Which behaviour best shows a candidate 'shaping meaning' in a discussion?
options: Dominating so nobody else can speak
Asking questions, making comments and drawing ideas together
Reading aloud from a prepared script
Agreeing with everything without adding anything
questions.explain: Interacting through suggestions, comments and questions to develop shared ideas is a key discussion skill.

questions.q: In a discussion, an effective candidate is expected to do which of the following?
options: Only listen and never speak
Both contribute ideas and respond to others
Speak continuously without pausing for others
Write down what others say instead of talking
questions.explain: Successful discussion involves both contributing and responding, interacting purposefully with the group.

questions.q: During a group discussion a quieter member has not yet spoken. What is the most effective interaction?
options: Ignore them and keep talking
Invite them in with a question such as 'What do you think?'
Tell them they are not allowed to speak
End the discussion early
questions.explain: Drawing others in through questions shows strong interaction and helps shape shared meaning.

questions.q: The Role Play task requires the candidate to do what?
options: Adopt and perform a role or character
Deliver a factual news report as themselves
Write a play script
Read a poem aloud
questions.explain: The role play task assesses the candidate's ability to create and sustain a role.

questions.q: What does it mean to 'sustain' a role in the role play task?
options: To change character several times for variety
To maintain the character consistently throughout the task
To perform for the shortest time possible
To speak only in your own voice
questions.explain: Sustaining a role means staying in character consistently, one of the assessed spoken skills.

questions.q: Which assessed skill is most directly targeted by the role play task?
options: Creating and sustaining different roles
Analysing a poem
Proofreading a document
Summarising statistics
questions.explain: The ability to create and sustain roles is the spoken language skill assessed through role play.

questions.q: A candidate is given the role of a town councillor arguing for a new park. Which is the strongest approach?
options: Speak entirely as themselves and ignore the role
Adopt the councillor's viewpoint and language, staying in character throughout
Refuse to take a position
Change into a different character halfway through
questions.explain: Convincingly adopting and consistently sustaining the assigned role is what the task rewards.

questions.q: How does role play extend a candidate's speaking skills beyond a straightforward presentation?
options: It requires them to speak and respond from a perspective other than their own
It removes the need to speak clearly
It is assessed only on written notes
It requires no interaction at all
questions.explain: Role play challenges candidates to convey meaning through an adopted character or viewpoint.

questions.q: What proportion of the overall CCEA GCSE English Language qualification does Unit 2: Speaking and Listening contribute?
questions.explain: Unit 2: Speaking and Listening is worth 20% of the overall CCEA GCSE English Language qualification.

questions.q: How is Unit 2: Speaking and Listening assessed in CCEA GCSE English Language?
options: By an external written examination sat under timed conditions
Internally assessed within the centre and moderated by CCEA
By a multiple-choice online test
It is not assessed and carries no marks
questions.explain: The speaking and listening tasks are assessed internally by the centre and externally moderated by CCEA.

questions.q: Which of these is an assessed spoken language skill across the Unit 2 tasks?
options: Speaking clearly and purposefully, adapting talk to audience and purpose
Correct spelling of technical terms
Neat handwriting
Reading speed in words per minute
questions.explain: Communicating clearly and adapting talk to situation, audience and purpose is a core assessed skill.

questions.q: A teacher asks candidates to 'take on the character of a witness being interviewed'. Which Unit 2 task is this?
options: Individual Presentation and Interaction
Discussion
Role Play
External written examination
questions.explain: Taking on and sustaining a character such as a witness is the role play task.

specSource: CCEA GCSE English Language (2017) specification; Unit 2: Speaking and Listening
